title: Extension criterion for torus, simple-root and Weyl maps
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $P=(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] with $|\Delta|\leq2$. Use the root homomorphisms $x_\gamma:\mathbf G_a\to U_\gamma\subseteq G$, simple Weyl representatives $n_\alpha$, reflections $s_\alpha$, and ordered positive-root subgroup $U^+$ of [lem-sfb-low-rank-universal-root-coordinates]. Let $H$ be an affine $A$-group scheme, meaning an affine scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ equipped with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Suppose given homomorphisms $f_T:T\to H$, $f_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\to H$ for $\alpha\in\Delta$, elements $h_\alpha\in H(A)$, and a homomorphism $F_+:U^+\to H$ such that $F_+\circ x_\alpha=f_\alpha$ at every simple root. Assume the following identities hold on points over every commutative $A$-algebra $R$:

1. For $t\in T(R)$ and $z\in R$, one has $f_T(t)f_\alpha(z)f_T(t)^{-1}=f_\alpha(\alpha(t)z)$ and $h_\alpha f_T(t)h_\alpha^{-1}=f_T(s_\alpha(t))$, where $s_\alpha:T\to T$ is the torus automorphism dual to the character-lattice reflection.
2. One has $h_\alpha^2=f_T(\alpha^\vee(-1))$ and $(h_\alpha f_\alpha(1))^3=1$. For distinct simple roots $\alpha,\beta$, put $m_{\alpha\beta}=\operatorname{ord}(s_\alpha s_\beta)$ and $t_{\alpha\beta}=(n_\alpha n_\beta)^{m_{\alpha\beta}}\in T(A)$. Require $(h_\alpha h_\beta)^{m_{\alpha\beta}}=f_T(t_{\alpha\beta})$.
3. For $\alpha\in\Delta$, $\gamma\in\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha\}$ and $z\in R$, one has
$$h_\alpha F_+(x_\gamma(z))h_\alpha^{-1}=F_+(n_\alpha x_\gamma(z)n_\alpha^{-1}).$$
Here $s_\alpha\gamma$ is positive in this case, so the argument of $F_+$ lies in $U^+$.

Then there is a unique $A$-group-scheme homomorphism $f:G\to H$ with $f|_T=f_T$, $f\circ x_\alpha=f_\alpha$, and $f(n_\alpha)=h_\alpha$ for every simple root. Uniqueness also holds when comparing any two already existing homomorphisms with these restrictions, without separately checking conditions 1--3. Rank zero and one are allowed, with the corresponding empty lists of conditions. All assertions allow nonreduced and disconnected $A$.

This is Conrad, Reductive Group Schemes, not an invocation of any SGA source. No Stacks tag states this group-theoretic input.

proof.text: If $\Delta=\varnothing$, the base condition forces $\Phi=\varnothing$: a root would be a nonzero integer combination of the empty base. The open-cell assertion of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] then identifies $T=\Omega$ as an open subscheme of $G$, and its surjective multiplication $T\times_A T\to G$ factors through $T\hookrightarrow G$. Thus this open immersion has image all of $G$, so is an isomorphism. The required extension is $f_T$ under $G=T$, and its torus restriction determines it uniquely.

source.place: Section 6.2 opening paragraph, p.198; rank-zero specialization.

proof.text: Assume $\Delta\ne\varnothing$. Identify the conventions of [lem-sfb-low-rank-universal-root-coordinates] with [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]: $z\mapsto\exp_\gamma(zX_\gamma)$ is $x_\gamma$, since both are equivariant closed homomorphisms with differential $1\mapsto X_\gamma$, and the former node gives uniqueness. The linked opposite generator, hence $n_\alpha$, is the same by the latter node's uniqueness. In particular $\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)=x_\alpha(1)$. The torus automorphisms $s_\alpha$ of the two nodes coincide: $s_\alpha(t)=t\alpha^\vee(\alpha(t))^{-1}$ induces $m\mapsto m-\langle m,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ on characters. The integers $m_{\alpha\beta}$ also agree: since $Z_G(T)=T$ by [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], an element of $N_G(T)/T$ acting trivially on $T$ is trivial, so the order of $s_\alpha s_\beta$ in that Weyl group equals its order as an automorphism of $T$, which is the integer of the item. Hence $t_{\alpha\beta}=(n_\alpha n_\beta)^{m_{\alpha\beta}}$ is the same element of $T(A)$ for both nodes' conventions, as used in step 3. Put $\bar f_\alpha=F_+|_{U_\alpha}$. For a pair of distinct simple roots, $\Delta=\{\alpha,\beta\}$, so the base sign condition gives $\Psi_{\alpha\beta}=\Phi^+$. The ordered-product descriptions in those nodes identify $U_{\Psi_{\alpha\beta}}=U^+$; take $q_{\alpha\beta}=F_+$. Its simple-root restrictions are $\bar f_\alpha,\bar f_\beta$, with $\bar f_\alpha\circ x_\alpha=f_\alpha$. In rank one no pair map is required.

The supplied identities verify the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-pinned-root-relations-hom-criterion]. The first identity gives torus equivariance for each $\bar f_\alpha$ and the reflection formula for $h_\alpha$; the root-coordinate parametrizations extend the displayed equalities from $x_\alpha(z)$ and $x_\gamma(z)$ to all points of the corresponding root subgroups over every $A$-algebra. The square relation is exactly $h_\alpha^2= f_T(\alpha^\vee(-1))$, while the cubic relation is the given $(h_\alpha f_\alpha(1))^3=1$ because $x_\alpha(1)=\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)$ and $F_+\circ x_\alpha=f_\alpha$. The pair relation is assumption 2. Finally, for $c\in\Psi_{\alpha\beta}\setminus\{\alpha\}$ (and symmetrically for $\beta$), assumption 3 gives the required conjugation identity for $q_{\alpha\beta}$; [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] ensures the conjugated point remains in $U_{\Psi_{\alpha\beta}}$. Therefore the criterion produces an $A$-group-scheme homomorphism $f:G\to H$ with the stated torus, simple-root and Weyl restrictions. Its restriction along $x_\alpha$ is $f_\alpha$ by construction.

For uniqueness, let $f,g:G\to H$ have the prescribed restrictions. Their restrictions to every $U_\alpha$ agree because the root maps $x_\alpha$ parametrise those root subgroups and $f\circ x_\alpha=g\circ x_\alpha=f_\alpha$; their restrictions to $T$ agree by hypothesis, and their values on $n_\alpha$ are both $h_\alpha$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-pinned-root-relations-hom-criterion] therefore gives $f=g$. All arguments use identities of points over arbitrary commutative $A$-algebras, so disconnected and nonreduced bases are included.

split_report.summary: No finished Lean declaration states this criterion.
